operations.description: A THIRD truncated failure path the first pass missed: the coverage runner's failure branch also printed `tail -10`. Found by the new test, not by re-reading -- which is the point of asserting the property (no short tail on a failure path) rather than patching the two sites I happened to notice. The SUCCESS branch keeps `tail -10`: a coverage summary is exactly what you want there.

edits.find:
log "WARN" "Coverage report failed: $output"
        echo "[post-implement] Coverage: FAILED"
        echo "$output" | tail -10
edits.replace:
log "WARN" "Coverage report failed: $output"
        echo "[post-implement] Coverage: FAILED"
        # 60, not 10: see the build/test paths above -- a failure's cause is not
        # in the last few lines of its own summary.
        echo "$output" | tail -60

operations.description: Two test defects of my own. (1) `_run_cycle` was handed a tmp subdirectory that was never created. (2) The PM assertion matched the literal string anywhere in the file, so it failed on the COMMENT explaining the removal -- a test that forbids naming the thing it removed cannot describe why. Now it asserts no ASSIGNMENT and no expansion.

edits.find:
text = (HOOKS / "session-start.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        assert "PM_INSTALL" not in text, "assigned eight times, read never (SC2034)"
        assert "PM_RUN" not in text
edits.replace:
text = (HOOKS / "session-start.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        # Assignments and expansions, not the bare name: the comment recording WHY
        # they were removed names them, and a test that forbids that is a test that
        # forbids the explanation.
        for var in ("PM_INSTALL", "PM_RUN"):
            assert not re.search(rf'^\s*{var}=', text, re.M), (
                f"{var} is assigned again; it was assigned eight times and read "
                "never (SC2034)")
            assert f"${var}" not in text and f"${{{var}}}" not in text
